[[Battle 4 Atlantis]] champions | tourney = [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Second Round }} {{2021–22 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 Baylor Bears men's basketball team''' represented [[Baylor University]] in the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], which was the Bears' 116th basketball season. The Bears, members of the [[Big 12 Conference]], played their home games at the [[Ferrell Center]] in [[Waco, Texas]]. They were led by 19th-year head coach [[Scott Drew]]. They finished the season 27–7, 14–4 in [[2021–22 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 Play]] to finish a tie for the regular season championship. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2022 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] to [[2021–22 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the East Region, where they defeated [[2021–22 Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball team|Norfolk State]] in the First Round before getting upset in the Second Round by [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. This was the first season in which the terms "men's" and "women's" are needed to distinguish Baylor's basketball teams. Before this season, Baylor women's basketball had used the nickname "Lady Bears", but on September 3, 2021, the school announced that basketball, soccer, and volleyball, the last three Baylor women's sports still using "Lady", would use only "Bears" from that point forward.{{cite news|url=https://www.kcentv.com/article/sports/baylor-drop-lady-bears-nickname-womens-teams/500-f3231efb-4cc2-401e-8c46-1529c8bf431a |title=Baylor University to drop 'Lady Bears' nickname from women's teams |first=Kurtis |last=Quillen |publisher=KCEN-TV |location=Temple, TX |date=September 3, 2021 |accessdate=September 4, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/womens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32143240/baylor-women-hoops-drops-lady-team-name-known-bears |title=Baylor women's hoops drops 'Lady' from team name, to be known as Bears |first=Mechelle |last=Voepel |website=ESPN.com |date=September 4, 2021 |accessdate=September 4, 2021}} ==Previous season== In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 Baylor Bears basketball team|Bears]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 28–2, 13–1 in [[2020–21 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 play]] to win the regular season championship. In the [[2021 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]], they defeated [[2020–21 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the quarterfinals{{Cite web|title=Kansas State vs. Baylor - Game Recap - March 11, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401301730|access-date=2021-07-22|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} before losing to [[2020–21 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Oklahoma State]] in the semifinals.{{Cite web|title=Oklahoma State inches closer to Big 12 Tournament title, but Baylor may benefit from upset loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/oklahoma-state-inches-closer-to-big-12-tournament-title-but-baylor-may-benefit-from-upset-loss/|access-date=2021-07-22|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the South region.{{Cite web|last=Werner|first=John|title=Baylor Bears No. 1 seed in NCAA tournament|url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/baylor-bears-no-1-seed-in-ncaa-tournament/article_eb25e4e8-8513-11eb-9d2d-5b2ad0711a03.html|access-date=2021-07-22|website=WacoTrib.com|language=en}} The Bears defeated [[2020–21 Hartford Hawks men's basketball team|Hartford]]{{Cite web|title=Hartford vs. Baylor -
